source_texts:
The Parable of the Sower
1 After this, __PERSON_F__ traveled about from one town and village to another, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of __MOST_HIGH_A__. The Twelve were with him, 2 and also some women who had been cured of evil spirits and diseases: __PERSON_D__ (called Magdalene) from whom seven demons had come out; 3 Joanna the wife of Chuza, the manager of __RULER_A__ household; Susanna; and many others. These women were helping to support them out of their own means.

4 While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to __PERSON_F__ from town after town, he told this parable: 5 “A farmer went out to sow his seed. As he was scattering the seed, some fell along the path; it was trampled on, and the birds ate it up. 6 Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the plants withered because they had no moisture. 7 Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the plants. 8 Still other seed fell on good soil. It came up and yielded a crop, a hundred times more than was sown.”

When he said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”

9 His disciples asked him what this parable meant. 10 He said, “The knowledge of the secrets of the kingdom of __MOST_HIGH_A__ has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that,

“‘though seeing, they may not see;
though hearing, they may not understand.’[a]

11 “This is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of __MOST_HIGH_A__. 12 Those along the path are the ones who hear, and then the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved. 13 Those on the rocky ground are the ones who receive the word with joy when they hear it, but they have no root. They believe for a while, but in the time of testing they fall away. 14 The seed that fell among thorns stands for those who hear, but as they go on their way they are choked by life’s worries, riches and pleasures, and they do not mature. 15 But the seed on good soil stands for those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, retain it, and by persevering produce a crop.

A Lamp on a Stand
16 “No one lights a lamp and hides it in a clay jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a stand, so that those who come in can see the light. 17 For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be known or brought out into the open. 18 Therefore consider carefully how you listen. Whoever has will be given more; whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken from them.”

__PERSON_F__ Mother and Brothers
19 Now __PERSON_F__ mother and brothers came to see him, but they were not able to get near him because of the crowd. 20 Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”

21 He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear __MOST_HIGH_A__ word and put it into practice.”

__PERSON_F__ Calms the Storm
22 One day __PERSON_F__ said to his disciples, “Let us go over to the other side of the lake.” So they got into a boat and set out. 23 As they sailed, he fell asleep. A squall came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.

24 The disciples went and woke him, saying, “Master, Master, we’re going to drown!”

He got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters; the storm subsided, and all was calm. 25 “Where is your faith?” he asked his disciples.

In fear and amazement they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him.”

__PERSON_F__ Restores a Demon-Possessed Man
26 They sailed to the region of the Gerasenes,[b] which is across the lake from __REGION_A__. 27 When __PERSON_F__ stepped ashore, he was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothes or lived in a house, but had lived in the tombs. 28 When he saw __PERSON_F__, he cried out and fell at his feet, shouting at the top of his voice, “What do you want with me, __PERSON_F__, Son of the __HONORED_A__ __MOST_HIGH_A__? I beg you, don’t torture me!” 29 For __PERSON_F__ had commanded the impure spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was chained hand and foot and kept under guard, he had broken his chains and had been driven by the demon into solitary places.

30 __PERSON_F__ asked him, “What is your name?”

“Legion,” he replied, because many demons had gone into him. 31 And they begged __PERSON_F__ repeatedly not to order them to go into the Abyss.

32 A large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside. The demons begged __PERSON_F__ to let them go into the pigs, and he gave them permission. 33 When the demons came out of the man, they went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.

34 When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, 35 and the people went out to see what had happened. When they came to __PERSON_F__, they found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at __PERSON_F__ feet, dressed and in his right mind; and they were afraid. 36 Those who had seen it told the people how the demon-possessed man had been cured. 37 Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked __PERSON_F__ to leave them, because they were overcome with fear. So he got into the boat and left.

38 The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to go with him, but __PERSON_F__ sent him away, saying, 39 “Return home and tell how much __MOST_HIGH_A__ has done for you.” So the man went away and told all over town how much __PERSON_F__ had done for him.

__PERSON_F__ Raises a Dead Girl and Heals a Sick Woman
40 Now when __PERSON_F__ returned, a crowd welcomed him, for they were all expecting him. 41 Then a man named Jairus, a synagogue leader, came and fell at __PERSON_F__ feet, pleading with him to come to his house 42 because his only daughter, a girl of about twelve, was dying.

As __PERSON_F__ was on his way, the crowds almost crushed him. 43 And a woman was there who had been subject to bleeding for twelve years,[c] but no one could heal her. 44 She came up behind him and touched the edge of his cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.

45 “Who touched me?” __PERSON_F__ asked.

When they all denied it, Peter said, “Master, the people are crowding and pressing against you.”

46 But __PERSON_F__ said, “Someone touched me; I know that power has gone out from me.”

47 Then the woman, seeing that she could not go unnoticed, came trembling and fell at his feet. In the presence of all the people, she told why she had touched him and how she had been instantly healed. 48 Then he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”

49 While __PERSON_F__ was still speaking, someone came from the house of Jairus, the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he said. “Don’t bother the teacher anymore.”

50 Hearing this, __PERSON_F__ said to Jairus, “Don’t be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”

51 When he arrived at the house of Jairus, he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter, __PERSON_C__ and James, and the child’s father and mother. 52 Meanwhile, all the people were wailing and mourning for her. “Stop wailing,” __PERSON_F__ said. “She is not dead but asleep.”

53 They laughed at him, knowing that she was dead. 54 But he took her by the hand and said, “My child, get up!” 55 Her spirit returned, and at once she stood up. Then __PERSON_F__ told them to give her something to eat. 56 Her parents were astonished, but he ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
translations:
播种的寓言
1 此后，__PERSON_F__ 从一个城池和乡村走到另一个地方，宣扬 __MOST_HIGH_A__ 国的福音。他的十二追随者和一些曾被邪灵和病症治愈的妇女也跟随他：2 有 __PERSON_D__（叫做抹大拉的），七个恶魔已从她身上出来；3 还有库萨的妻子约亚拿，库萨是 __RULER_A__ 家中的家臣；苏撒拿以及许多其他妇女。这些妇女用自己的财物帮助供养他们。

4 当人群聚集，许多人从城里乡村赶来找 __PERSON_F__ 时，他讲了这个寓言：5 “有个农夫出去播种。播种的时候，有些种子落在路旁，野鸟吃掉了；6 有些落在岩石地上，刚发芽的时候因为没有水分，植物枯萎了；刺藤一起长起，挤住了植物；8 还有一些落在肥沃土里，发芽生长，结出百倍的收成。”

他说完，就喊道：“有耳可听的，就应当听。”

10 他回答说：但我对别人讲寓言，为的是

‘他们虽看见，却不看见；
虽听见，却不明白。’[a]

11 “这寓言的意思是：种子就是 __MOST_HIGH_A__ 的话语。12 路旁的种子是那些听见了，使他们不信、不得救。13 岩石地上的种子，是那些听见时欢喜接受的话，却没有根基。但试炼时就跌倒了。14 落在刺藤里的种子代表那些听了，却被生活的忧虑、财富和享乐挤住，不能成熟。15 落在好土里的种子，是那些心地善良纯洁的人，听见并领受话语，持守到底就结出果实。

灯架上的火炬
16 “没有人点火炬后把它藏在陶器里，17 反而放在灯架上，让进来的人能看见光。因为隐藏的事必被揭露，隐藏的秘密必被知道、显露出来。18 因此，你们要留心听。有的人有，就还要给他；没有的人，连他以为有的也要夺去。”

__PERSON_F__ 的妈妈和弟兄
19 当时，__PERSON_F__ 的妈妈和弟兄来要见他，却因人群拥堵进不了。20 有人告诉他：“你的妈妈和弟兄站在外面，想见你。”

21 他回答说：“我的妈妈和弟兄就是听 __MOST_HIGH_A__ 话并遵行的人。”

__PERSON_F__ 平息风浪
22 有一天，__PERSON_F__ 对追随者说：“我们渡到海对岸去吧。他睡着了。突然，一阵狂风袭海，舟差点被淹没，大家十分危险。

24 追随者去叫醒他，说：“老师，老师，我们要淹死了！”

他起来斥责风和狂浪，风浪就止息，25 他问追随者：”

追随者既惧怕又惊奇，彼此说：“这是谁？连风和水也听从他了！”

__PERSON_F__ 赶出被魔鬼附的人
26 他们来到格拉森人的地区，[b] 在海的对岸。27 __PERSON_F__ 上了岸，就遇见一个被魔附体的男人，不穿衣服，也不住屋子，只住在坟墓里。28 见到 __PERSON_F__，他喊叫着，跪伏在他脚下，大声说：至高 __HONORED_A__ __MOST_HIGH_A__ 的儿子啊，我求你，不要折磨我！”29 因为 __PERSON_F__ 曾吩咐那污灵从他身上出来。那魔鬼多次附着他，虽用铁链锁住，他仍挣断束缚，被魔鬼驱使到旷野去。

30 __PERSON_F__ 询问：“你叫什么名字？”他说，因为许多魔鬼附在他身上。31 魔鬼多次请求 __PERSON_F__ 不要吩咐他们进去深渊。

32 那里山岭上有一大群野猪吃草。魔鬼求 __PERSON_F__ 允许它们进入野猪群，__PERSON_F__ 便允许。33 魔鬼出来后，进入野猪群，那野猪一起奔下陡坡，掉进海里淹死了。

34 牧猪者看到这事，就逃跑报信村里和城内，35 众人出来见 __PERSON_F__，见那魔鬼出去的人坐在 __PERSON_F__ 脚前，穿着衣服，神志清醒，就恐惧了。36 曾看到的人将魔鬼赶出时所发生的事告诉众人。求 __PERSON_F__ 离开，

38 那被魔鬼赶出的人请求跟随他，__PERSON_F__ 却遣送他回去，说：39 “回家去，”那人就走遍全城，宣扬 __PERSON_F__ 为他所作的一切。

__PERSON_F__ 叫死去的女孩复活，并医治病妇
40 __PERSON_F__ 返回时，有许多人迎接，因为他们都等着他。41 有一个名叫亚伊鲁的会堂官员，来到 __PERSON_F__ 脚前求他去他家，42 因为他唯一女儿大约十岁，快要死了。

43 __PERSON_F__ 正走时，人群几乎把他挤倒。44 有个血漏病十二年的妇女在那里，先前无人医治她；触碰了他的袍角，血马上停了。

45 __PERSON_F__ 问：“谁摸了我？”

大家都否认，彼得说：“老师，众人拥挤推搡你。”

46 __PERSON_F__ 道：“有人摸我，我知道有能力从我身上出去。”

47 那女人见无法隐瞒，颤抖着来，跪伏在他脚下，在众人面前讲述为何触碰他，如何立刻被治愈。48 他对她说：“女儿，你的信念拯救了你，安然离去吧。”

49 当 __PERSON_F__ 还说话时，说：“你的女儿死了，别再烦扰老师了。”

50 听见这话，__PERSON_F__ 对亚伊鲁说：“别害怕，只需信，她必然得救。”

除彼得、__PERSON_C__ 和雅各，还有孩子的父母，都禁止任何人入内。52 众人为女孩哭喊悲号，“不要哭，她并非死亡，只是沉睡。”

53 他们讥笑他，因为知道女孩死了。54 他握住女孩的手说：“孩子，起来！”55 她的魂魄归来，马上起身。__PERSON_F__ 命令给她食物。56 她的父母惊奇，他叮嘱他们保密发生的事。
